# Argus Landscape Refresh — Decision-Grade Report (2026-06-13)

*Scope: declarative, Kubernetes-native, PREVENTIVE enforcement of agent behavioral invariants (per-run step cap, cumulative USD budget kill-switch, input-hash dedup) + named runaway-pattern detection (RetryStorm / RateSpike / RecursionLoop).*

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Niche Verdict

**Verdict: the gap is still OPEN, but it has NARROWED materially since 2026-05-11. Confidence: HIGH that the *exact* combination Argus targets is still unshipped anywhere; MEDIUM-HIGH that it remains defensible for 6–12 months.**

The precise niche — *a single declarative Kubernetes CRD that enforces agent run-scoped behavioral invariants (step cap + cumulative USD budget kill + input-hash dedup) backed by named sliding-window runaway-pattern detection* — is occupied by **no shipping tool**. The named patterns RetryStorm/RateSpike/RecursionLoop appear in **no competitor product**, and input-hash dedup-as-a-kill-switch is absent everywhere as a declarative K8s invariant ([github.com/defilantech/infercost](https://github.com/defilantech/infercost)).

**Single most important finding (the headline delta):** LiteLLM has, in its `main` branch, shipped **two of Argus's three core invariants as hard-blocking 429 controls** — a per-run step cap (`max_iterations`) and a cumulative per-session USD budget kill-switch (`max_budget_per_session`) — and it implements them with **almost exactly Argus's planned mechanism**: an async pre-call hook over a Redis Lua atomic counter on a DualCache (in-memory + Redis) ([max_iterations_limiter.py](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/proxy/hooks/max_iterations_limiter.py), [max_budget_per_session_limiter.py](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/proxy/hooks/max_budget_per_session_limiter.py), [docs.litellm.ai/docs/a2a_iteration_budgets](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/a2a_iteration_budgets)). This is the most important fact for the build phase: **the "nobody enforces invariants on agent behavior" one-liner is no longer defensible** and must be retired before any public launch.

**What keeps the niche open:** every existing implementation is missing at least one structural axis Argus owns — (a) it is **imperative gateway config, not a portable K8s CRD**; (b) it is **vendor-bound** (LiteLLM's session budget requires its own `agent_id` registry and only sees LiteLLM traffic); (c) it is **static threshold caps, not sliding-window PATTERN/anomaly detection** (RetryStorm and RateSpike have *no analog anywhere*); and (d) **input-hash dedup as a runaway kill-switch does not exist** (LiteLLM only has cost-saving response caching).

**The required pivot:** reposition from "first to cap agents" to "the **declarative, vendor-neutral, K8s-native, pattern-detecting** invariant layer." Lead with the two axes nobody has — **per-run pattern detection (RetryStorm/RateSpike)** and **input-hash dedup** — and frame the USD budget as *one of three correlated invariants in one CRD*, not the headline.

## 2. What Changed Since 2026-05-11

Concrete deltas against the month-old assumptions:

1. **LiteLLM colonized 2 of 3 invariants (biggest change).** "Agent Iteration Budgets" now ship `max_iterations` (step cap, 429) and `max_budget_per_session` (USD kill, 429), Redis-backed, in releases **v1.88.1 (2026-06-09)**, with a **v1.84.8 backport landing today 2026-06-13** and **v1.89.0-rc.2 (2026-06-10)** in flight ([litellm releases](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases), [a2a_iteration_budgets](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/a2a_iteration_budgets)). It also has an **Agentic Loop Hook** with identical-fingerprint loop-abort + max-reruns ([agentic_loop_hook](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/agentic_loop_hook)).
2. **GAIE built the blocking *plumbing* but not the policy.** PR #2637 (merged **2026-03-26**) lets EPP/BBR plugins return Envoy `ImmediateResponse` to **block** requests — explicitly for "guardrails" ([PR #2637](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/pull/2637)). v1.5.0 (**2026-04-19**) shipped a Flow Control admission layer (priority/fairness/Saturation Detector/503 load-shedding) — but **infrastructure-load-based, not cost/budget/behavior** ([priority-and-capacity](https://gateway-api-inference-extension.sigs.k8s.io/concepts/priority-and-capacity/)). The community **let the per-user rate-limit plugin (#1912) auto-close as "rotten" on 2026-04-27** and **rejected the usage-limit PR #2268 unmerged** ([issue #1912](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/issues/1912)).
3. **kagent → still a runtime, no enforcement.** Latest **v0.9.7 (2026-06-11)**; recent work is BYO-agent deploy, agents-as-MCP, context compaction — **no budget/loop/step-cap/dedup features** ([kagent releases](https://github.com/kagent-dev/kagent/releases)). It delegates guardrails to kgateway (content moderation + token rate-limit only) and added an **Agent Sandbox CRD (isolation, not behavior)**. CNCF maturity unchanged: Sandbox since 2025-05-22 ([cncf.io/projects/kagent](https://www.cncf.io/projects/kagent/)).
4. **llm-d → still inference serving.** **v0.7.0 (2026-05-12)** made a **standalone generic proxy the DEFAULT deployment** (validates Argus's standalone-proxy Tap), plus a breaking CUDA 13.0.2 bump; **CNCF Sandbox accepted 2026-03-24** ([llm-d v0.7.0](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/releases/tag/v0.7.0), [CNCF blog](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/03/24/welcome-llm-d-to-the-cncf-evolving-kubernetes-into-sota-ai-infrastructure/)). It explicitly disclaims policy: *"llm-d does not need to reinvent gateway functionality, security policy, or Kubernetes networking APIs"* ([agentgateway integration](https://agentgateway.dev/blog/2026-03-19-agentgateway-llm-d-gaie-inference-serving/)).
5. **InferCost → still observe-only, but enforcement now on the roadmap.** **v0.5.0 (2026-06-04)**, Apache-2.0, K8s operator with `CostProfile`/`UsageReport` CRDs; "Enforce" is **"Planned"** and `TokenBudget` is **"coming soon"** ([github.com/defilantech/infercost](https://github.com/defilantech/infercost), [infercost.ai](https://infercost.ai/)). **This is the closest structural collision and a fast-follower threat.**
6. **agentgateway emerged as the closest K8s-native budget competitor.** A **"kill switch"** blog (2026-02-21) markets per-agent token-per-minute hard caps + `kubectl scale … --replicas=0` ([kill-switch blog](https://agentgateway.dev/blog/2026-02-21-kill-switch/)); a Solo.io reference impl adds a **dollar-denominated budget kill-switch** (reserve-then-settle, ImmediateResponse on exhaustion) ([solo.io blog](https://www.solo.io/blog/building-real-time-ai-cost-controls-with-agentgateway)). Donated to the **Linux Foundation / Agentic AI Foundation**, Apache-2.0, GEP-713-conformant CRDs.
7. **Cloudflare AI Gateway shipped preventive $ spend limits** (block with 429 or reroute to a cheaper model), **public beta ~2026-06-05** — but **edge SaaS, not K8s/CRD** ([spend-limits docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/spend-limits/)).
8. **Envoy AI Gateway v0.7.0 (2026-06-04)** added **quota-aware rate limiting**; CRDs graduated to v1beta1 in v0.6.0 (2026-05-05) ([release notes](https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/release-notes/)).
9. **Two near-identical CNCF Sandbox applicants were DECLINED** for lack of community: **SemaMesh** ("Layer 8 Governance for Autonomous AI Agents," agent loop detection + financial quotas, declined **2026-03-06**, [#455](https://github.com/cncf/sandbox/issues/455)) and **OPAL** ("Outcome-Predictive Agent Layer," built on kagent, declined **2026-06-01**, [#492](https://github.com/cncf/sandbox/issues/492)). The niche is **contested in spirit, but the slot is empty**.
10. **The problem narrative got stronger and fresher** — see §4.
11. **Toolchain moved:** Go **1.26.4**, Kubebuilder **v4.14.0**, controller-runtime latest **v0.24.1**, K8s **1.35** ([kubebuilder releases](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder/releases)).
12. **Prempti** (Falco ecosystem, announced **2026-05-20**) — preventive AI-coding-agent tool-call policy, but **Falco YAML rules, not a K8s CRD** ([CNCF blog](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/05/20/introducing-prempti-policy-and-visibility-for-ai-coding-agents/)).
13. **Standards crystallized:** GEP-713 Policy Attachment is the de-facto CRD shape, and is **already applied to LLM governance** by agentgateway (`AgentgatewayPolicy`) and kgateway (`TrafficPolicy`) ([GEP-713](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/geps/gep-713/), [agentgateway rate-limit](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/2.2.x/llm/rate-limit/)).

**Bottom line:** preventive enforcement now clearly exists, split across (a) K8s-native gateways that cap *token-rate / $ budget* but lack agent-run behavior invariants, and (b) SaaS/SDK products that do budget+loop but aren't declarative K8s CRDs. **Argus's exact four-element combination (declarative K8s CRD × behavioral invariants × named pattern detection × input-hash dedup) is shipped by no one.**

**Install commands:**
```bash
# Go 1.26.4
curl -fsSL https://go.dev/dl/go1.26.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz | sudo tar -C /usr/local -xz
export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin

# Kubebuilder v4.14.0
curl -L -o kubebuilder https://go.kubebuilder.io/dl/v4.14.0/$(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH)
chmod +x kubebuilder && sudo mv kubebuilder /usr/local/bin/

# Scaffold
kubebuilder init --domain argus.dev --repo github.com/<org>/argus
kubebuilder create api --group policy --version v1alpha1 --kind RunawayPolicy --resource --controller

# Redis 8.8.0 (dev) — or Valkey 8.x
docker run -d --name argus-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:8.8.0
```

**ext_proc note:** the **core gRPC ext_proc filter + `immediate_response` block path is stable and safe to build on now**; only the newer sub-features (`http_service`, `processing_request_modifier`, `on_processing_response`) carry the alpha/WIP warning — avoid depending on those for v0.1.

## 6. Tap / Integration Recommendation

**Build order for v0.1: (1) Standalone HTTP proxy FIRST → (2) LiteLLM callback → (3) ext_proc / EnvoyExtensionPolicy.** All three behind **one transport-agnostic decision engine** so each Tap is a thin adapter, not a fork of the detection logic.

**Build the standalone HTTP reverse-proxy Tap first** (covering **both** OpenAI-compatible *and* the Anthropic Messages API), because:
- It is the **only mode that is simultaneously vendor-neutral and Envoy-free**, so it runs end-to-end on a laptop for **demo day** without standing up Envoy Gateway (which is heavy and whose `EnvoyExtensionPolicy` is v1alpha1) ([dataplane caveats](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/tasks/extensibility/ext-proc/)).
- It sees the **full request body** (model + messages) needed for **input-hash dedup, step counting, and budget accounting** — header-only modes can't do dedup.
- It covers the **widest framework surface**: LangChain/LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK (`set_default_openai_client`), AutoGen/AG2, CrewAI non-native, and ADK-via-LiteLlm all route through a configurable `base_url`; a **co-equal Anthropic Messages API tap (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`)** is required because the **Claude Agent SDK and CrewAI-native Anthropic/Gemini bypass LiteLLM** — so a LiteLLM callback alone is structurally insufficient.
- llm-d v0.7.0 making a **standalone generic proxy the default** validates this in-path topology for real clusters ([llm-d v0.7.0](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/releases/tag/v0.7.0)).

**Build the LiteLLM callback second** — it is the **fastest-to-demo** mode where LiteLLM is already deployed, and it is *idiomatic*: implement a thin `CustomLogger` subclass with `async_pre_call_hook` (block by raising) + `async_log_success_event` (accumulate), **mirroring LiteLLM's own `max_budget_per_session_limiter.py`** ([call_hooks](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/call_hooks), [custom_guardrail](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/guardrails/custom_guardrail)). Note LiteLLM is **substrate, not just competitor** — its hook API *is* this Tap.

**Build the ext_proc / `EnvoyExtensionPolicy` Tap third** — it is the **flagship "K8s-native" production mode** and the right CNCF story (shared, GA-adjacent surface with GAIE + Envoy AI Gateway, true `immediate_response` blocking), but it's deferred because it requires an Envoy Gateway deployment and rides a v1alpha1 CRD. Make **fail-open vs fail-closed an explicit `RunawayPolicy` knob** and keep a header-only fast path when no body inspection is needed.

---

## 7. CRD Design Alignment

**Recommendation: keep a standalone `RunawayPolicy` CRD, but make it GEP-713-conformant. Do NOT invent a novel policy-attachment shape; do NOT try to land inside GAIE (which has explicitly *not* built behavior policy).**

Concretely:
1. **Conform to GEP-713 Policy Attachment** (status: *Memorandum* — it formalizes the existing community pattern): the name `RunawayPolicy` already fits the `xPolicy` convention; move targets into a **`targetRefs` list in `spec`** (group/kind/name/sectionName), and add a **status stanza with `Accepted`/`Programmed` conditions** ([GEP-713](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/geps/gep-713/)). This is the *same* mechanism agentgateway (`AgentgatewayPolicy`) and kgateway (`TrafficPolicy`) already use for LLM policy ([agentgateway rate-limit docs](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/2.2.x/llm/rate-limit/)).
2. **Semantics: use Inherited (GEP-2649) as the primary class** so a namespace- or Gateway-scoped budget/step-cap **cascades** to HTTPRoutes / InferencePools; reserve **Direct (GEP-2648)** for per-route overrides.
3. **`targetRefs` should attach to a Gateway / HTTPRoute / InferencePool** (gateway-tap modes) **and/or a workload/namespace** (proxy/LiteLLM modes).
4. **Align step/call/token vocabulary with OpenTelemetry GenAI semconv** (status: Development): define **"a call" = one `gen_ai.operation` `chat` span**; **"a step" = `invoke_agent` child spans** (`chat`/`execute_tool`/`plan`); account budgets on `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`; emit metrics named to mirror `gen_ai.client.token.usage` so Argus is drop-in for existing GenAI dashboards ([gen-ai-agent-spans](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md), [gen-ai-metrics](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics.md)).
5. **The cumulative USD budget is a genuine wedge** — implement it as a **first-class feature with a configurable token→USD price table**, because **OTel defines no USD metric and agentgateway only does token-based limits with externally-estimated cost** ([gen-ai-metrics](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics.md)). Do not ship it as a re-skin of token rate-limiting.

**Net:** reuse the policy-CRD *plumbing* (GEP-713 + OTel GenAI), differentiate on the **behavioral invariants nobody has standardized**.

---

## 8. Risks & Required Pivots

**Positioning pivots (mandatory before any public claim):**
- **Retire "Nobody enforces invariants on agent behavior."** It is now false in spirit: LiteLLM (step cap + $ kill), agentgateway ($ kill-switch), Cloudflare ($ spend limits), and Anthropic SDK (`maxBudgetUsd`) all preventively enforce *some* invariant. **Reframe** to: *declarative, vendor-neutral, Kubernetes-native enforcement of run-scoped behavioral invariants (steps, dedup, cumulative budget) plus named runaway-pattern detection.*
- **Lead with the two axes nobody has:** **sliding-window PATTERN detection (RetryStorm + RateSpike)** — which have *no analog anywhere* — and **input-hash dedup as a kill-switch.** Treat RecursionLoop and step-cap as "table stakes that LiteLLM partially does — we make them declarative + K8s-native + cross-vendor."
- **Don't pitch "the only step cap":** every framework already ships an in-process one (LangGraph 25, CrewAI 25 — though [issue #3847](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/issues/3847) shows it doesn't reliably halt, OpenAI Agents SDK 10, AG2 10, ADK LoopAgent none-by-default, Anthropic `maxBudgetUsd`). Pitch **external, default-on, cumulative, cross-run** enforcement that in-process opt-in caps can't deliver.

**Niche-narrowing threats to monitor (re-verify before each milestone):**
- **InferCost** (highest priority): same Apache-2.0 K8s-operator/cost-CRD lane, with `TokenBudget` "coming soon" and "Enforce" "Planned." Decide explicitly: **interop** (InferCost = cost truth via DCGM; Argus = enforcement) **or compete** — before building TokenBudget-like features ([infercost](https://github.com/defilantech/infercost)).
- **agentgateway**: incumbent in the K8s-native enforcement lane with a dollar kill-switch and GEP-713 CRDs; ride the AAIF/CNCF rails rather than compete head-on on gateway rate-limiting.
- **LiteLLM**: ships daily backports; watch v1.89.x for any move toward a CRD or anomaly-pattern guardrails.
- **GAIE**: watch issues #1912/#2268 and the proposals dir — if declarative per-user/cost/budget limits revive, the gap narrows.

**Ecosystem/process risks:**
- **CNCF Sandbox is community-gated, NOT novelty-gated.** Two near-identical agent-governance projects (SemaMesh, OPAL) were **declined solely for lack of community/adopters** ([#455](https://github.com/cncf/sandbox/issues/455), [#492](https://github.com/cncf/sandbox/issues/492)). **Do not target Sandbox at first commit** — plan 6–12 months of multi-org adoption first; a qualifying single-vendor project (HolmesGPT) still took ~3–4 months *after* it had traction. Build the form artifacts (ADOPTERS, MAINTAINERS, SECURITY, CoC, CONTRIBUTING, roadmap, Apache-2.0) into the repo from day one ([application.yml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cncf/sandbox/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/application.yml)). Seriously weigh the TOC's standing advice to **merge with / land as a subproject of** kagent or GAIE.
- **Name collision:** pending Sandbox app **"AI Runway" (#488)** is phonetically close to Argus's "Agent Runaway Detector" ([#488](https://github.com/cncf/sandbox/issues/488)). Resolve branding early.
- **Don't over-claim on evidence:** avoid the $500M Axios figure, the "invisible tokens" claim, and the non-existent hook-recursion postmortem (§4) — a reviewer who checks will find them unverified.

## 10. Open Questions (need a human decision)

1. **InferCost — compete or interop?** It's the closest structural collision (Apache-2.0 K8s cost-operator with `TokenBudget`/Enforce on the roadmap). Decide before building budget features: position InferCost as the cost-truth feed (DCGM) into Argus enforcement, or build the price-table budget independently?
2. **Standalone bid vs. subproject?** The CNCF TOC's standing advice ("merge with another current project") plus two declined lookalikes suggests landing as a **subproject of / tight integration with kagent or GAIE** would lower the community bar. Standalone Argus, or ride existing adoption?
3. **Branding:** resolve the "AI Runway" (#488) phonetic collision — keep "Argus / Agent Runaway Detector" or rename?
4. **USD as headline or supporting invariant?** Given agentgateway/LiteLLM/Cloudflare now do budget kills, is the cumulative-USD kill-switch a co-equal pillar or explicitly demoted behind pattern-detection + dedup in all messaging?
5. **Anthropic API tap priority:** is a co-equal Anthropic Messages API tap in scope for v0.1 (needed for Claude Agent SDK / CrewAI-native), or deferred — accepting a coverage gap on Anthropic-native traffic for the demo?
6. **Fail-open vs fail-closed default** for the data-plane Taps when the engine/Redis is unreachable — a safety-vs-availability call that affects positioning ("we never let a runaway through" vs "we never block legitimate traffic").
7. **CNCF timing:** accept that Sandbox is a 6–12-month *downstream* goal (post-adoption), and that the demo-day v0.1 is a *community-seeding* milestone, not a Sandbox-application milestone?

### Build-readiness gaps to resolve BEFORE W3 (design spike)
1. **Run / session identity correlation** — the linchpin of every "per-run" invariant in a vendor-neutral tap. How Argus derives a stable run-id from arbitrary frameworks / the standalone proxy / A2A hops is undesigned (only LiteLLM's `x-litellm-trace-id` precedent surfaced).
2. **Streaming & pre-call cost gating** — providers report token usage post-call and responses stream; how Argus accounts/blocks mid-stream and estimates USD *before* a call (everyone else is "best-effort") is unanalyzed.
3. **What exactly gets hashed for dedup / RecursionLoop** — full messages array? last user turn? And how tool-call recursion is reconstructed from OpenAI/Anthropic bodies vs intercepting MCP.
4. **Redis sliding-window engine design** — Lua atomic counters, TTLs, multi-replica consistency, failure modes (single point of failure for the kill-switch). Asserted by analogy to LiteLLM, not designed.
5. **Pattern declarability** — `RunawayPolicy` currently has no fields to tune RetryStorm/RateSpike/RecursionLoop windows; the novel pattern matcher has no declarative surface yet.
6. **USD price-table sourcing** — LiteLLM already ships a reusable `model_prices_and_context_window.json`; decide reuse vs build.
7. **Redis 8.x licensing** — for an Apache-2.0 / CNCF-bound project, evaluate Valkey 8.x as a first-class alternative, not a footnote.

### Missing topics (lower priority, but CNCF-relevant)
Inline-enforcement latency benchmark · security threat model + evasion vectors (agent rotating run-ids to defeat caps) · A2A/JSON-RPC inter-agent correlation · HA/state durability · adoption-seeding GTM motion · real **"Argus" name-availability search** (only the CNCF "AI Runway" #488 phonetic clash was checked).

- "**$500M Claude bill in one month**" — single anonymous source via Axios; present as "reported," never fact.
- "**Invisible ~20K server-side tokens / 40% billing inflation**" — AI-written blogs, Anthropic never confirmed.
- "**Anthropic hook-recursion postmortem**" — does not exist (hallucinated conflation). The real 2026-04-23 postmortem names an idle-session cache-clearing bug.
- The **$47K** and **$4,200** postmortems — illustrative community anecdotes only; the $47K weekly figures sum to ~$25.7K, not $47K. Never cite as corporate incidents.

## Appendix B — Adversarial verdicts (the 4 load-bearing claims)

All four claims survived ("refuted = false"), but with nuance:

1. **GAIE/Gateway API has no behavior-enforcement policy** → holds (weak refutation). Niche = **NARROW**, not closed: the blocking *plumbing* (ext_proc `ImmediateResponse`) now exists, but the cost/budget/behavior *policy* does not.
2. **kagent / llm-d / InferCost don't preventively enforce behavior invariants** → **VERIFIED, holds cleanly** (no refutation). This specific framing is still true.
3. **LiteLLM does spend budgets but not K8s-native runaway-pattern detection** → holds (weak refutation). LiteLLM now ships step-cap + per-session $ kill + an Agentic Loop Hook, so tighten the wording: Argus's edge is *declarative + K8s-native + cross-vendor + sliding-window pattern detection*, not "first to cap."
4. **The cost-runaway problem is real and ongoing in 2026** → **validated**. Lean on the dated primaries (Fortune/Uber COO on-record 2026-05-26; TechCrunch 2026-06-05), not the anecdotes.

**Positioning consequence:** the literal one-liner ("Nobody enforces invariants on agent behavior") is true *about kagent/llm-d* but false *in spirit* now that LiteLLM/agentgateway/Cloudflare/Anthropic-SDK each enforce *some* invariant. Retire/reframe it (see §8).
